newsitem.title: SAUDI ARABIA: Malaysian premier receives Saudi Islamic award.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian premier receives Saudi Islamic award.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's Defence Minister Prince Sultan presented King Faisal Foundation international awards to Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad, an Iraqi scholar and five Western scientists at a ceremony in Riyadh.
"This evening ... we celebrate the accomplishments of the human mind," Prince Khalid bin Faisal told a packed audience of men in traditional gold-edged robes at the Saturday night event.

Prince Khalid, son of the late King Faisal, is chairman of the board for the annual King Faisal International Prize, first awarded in 1979 and considered one of the most prestigious prizes in the Arab world.
Mahathir, who arrived in the oil-rich kingdom on Friday and performed a pilgrimage to the Moslem holy city of Mecca, received the prize for services to Islam.

The foundation said it had awarded the prize to the Malaysian leader because "his wisdom and moderation as prime minister of Malaysia have reflected the magnanimity and forebearance of Islam ... and (his) policies have fostered rapport and cooperation between Malaysian Moslems and non-Moslems".
Mahathir said: "The success of the Malaysians owes a lot to Islam as a way of life."
The prize for Islamic studies went to 80-year-old Iraqi scholar Abdul Karim Zedan Biej for his 11-volume study on the status of women in Islam.
The prize for medicine was shared by professors Colin Masters of Australia, Konrad Beyreuther of Germany and Canadian James Gusella for studies on degenerative diseases of the nervous system.
Americans Carl Wieman and Eric Cornell, both physicists at the University of Colorado, shared the science award for achieving a new state of matter.
This year's awards bring the total number of laureates to 118 from 32 countries. Winners receive a cash endowment of $200,000 while co-winners share the grant.
King Faisal, who ascended to the throne in 1964, was killed by a deranged nephew in 1975. The Riyadh-based King Faisal Foundation is dedicated to philanthropic activities.
